claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially in a high-temperature BCC state.
Phase diversity during cooling and subsequent thermal exposure arises from kinetically driven local compositional fluctuations.
Local compositional fluctuations promote short-range ordering.
Short-range-ordered regions serve as precursors for nucleation of secondary phases.
Rapid quenching preserves the high-temperature BCC state with minimal ordering and compositional fluctuation.
Slower cooling permits localized compositional inhomogeneities to form.
Slower cooling permits short-range order to develop within localized compositional inhomogeneities.
Localized compositional inhomogeneities act as nucleation sites for secondary phases during subsequent thermal exposure.
Relative to rapid quenching, slower cooling followed by a moderate isothermal hold will produce greater nanoscale compositional heterogeneity.
Relative to rapid quenching, slower cooling followed by a moderate isothermal hold will produce more early-stage ordering.
The increased heterogeneity and ordering in the slowly cooled and held sample will lead to the onset of secondary-phase nucleation.
The proposed mechanism should apply at intermediate cooling rates and during moderate thermal holds.
Cooling that is too rapid suppresses ordering.
The proposed mechanism should not remain observable after thermal exposure long enough to attain full equilibrium.
TEM, XRD, and APT can be used to compare microstructure, phase identity, and nanoscale compositional fluctuations between the treatments.
